title.narrative: Participatory Citywide Urban Upgrading (PCWUU) in Egypt – Phase 2

description.narrative: The Egyptian government has prioritized addressing unsafe and informal settlements among its crucial plans and actions. In 2020, cooperation between UN-Habitat and the Informal settlement Development Fund (ISDF) under the first phase of this programme (2017-2022) resulted in the change of name and mandate of the fund, now known as the Urban Development Fund (UDF). The project aims to provide innovative urban regeneration tools and approaches to reduce inequalities and improve living conditions in urban areas in Egypt. Building on the national endorsement of the comprehensive concept of the first phase of the project “Participatory urban upgrading in Egypt”, this second phase aims to support the new national Urban Development Fund (UDF) to effectively implement its new mandate through three main outcome areas i) improved capacities, tools and methodologies for effective upgrading and development of identified urban development areas; ii) encouraged civil society, private sectors and key stakeholders to contribute to development activities within effective participatory and inclusive development frameworks; and iii) advanced positioning of Urban Development Funds and enhance opportunities for national and international cooperation for technical and financial support to the urban development sector in Egypt and the Arab region. In this second phase (2022- 2027), the project will work closely with the UDF and all relevant stakeholders to adopt and implement this new approach effectively. This will entail provision of institutional and capacity support to the UDF team to formulate and implement their new role effectively. This also includes supporting innovative and smart management cycle of the UDF mandate: planning, financing, implementing, monitoring, and reporting. Additionally, the new phase will support identification and implementation of priority development interventions based on the Participatory citywide urban development plans. The project will provide effective tools and methodologies to ensure financial, social and environmental feasibility and innovate financing mechanisms for the identified development projects. Finally, the project will also support communicating and advocacy for the new fund identity to ensure effective cooperation with all development partners, and to position the fund as a unique centre of excellence for urban upgrading and development in Egypt and the Arab countries. The project is also implemented in cooperation with the General Organization for Physical Planning (GOPP) within a framework that integrates various policies and approaches adopted by the Egyptian government to face the challenges of informal urban sprawl and inadequate housing. Additionally, the project is in line with the recommendations of the new National Housing Strategy that was published in 2020 in cooperation between the Ministry of Housing, Utilities and Urban Communities (MoHUUC) and UN-Habitat in Egypt. The strategy illustrated a more progressive understanding of the concept of urban development areas; suggesting that these areas are not limited to unplanned areas (informal settlements) only, but rather extending its scope to include: all areas that are not currently fully utilized in terms of their existing potentials and require intervention to optimize its exploitation in an integrated manner.
